newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson helps pull Swedish shares to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson helps pull Swedish shares to lower close.

text.p: A fall in heavyweight telecoms group Ericsson helped pull Swedish share prices lower on Tuesday.
The Stockholm general index fell 0.77 percent to 3,148.13 in turnover of 3.45 billion crowns.

Swedish/U.S. drugs company Pharmacia & Upjohn was in focus after releasing second quarter earnings. The share reversed afternoon losses when New York opened and rose four crowns to 298 in Stockholm, despite analysts worrying about sluggish sales for new products.
Car safety equipment company Autoliv slid.

Autoliv, which presented six-month earnings a day earlier, was the most traded share and fell 12 crowns to 283.5 on worries about price pressure in the U.S. and uncertainty about merger costs. But analysts were not too concerned, saying they would keep their earnings estimates unchanged.
Ericsson fell five crowns to 354 on profit taking after rocketing on strong second quarter figures last week.
"It could be reasonable to do some profit-taking after the strong surge last week. I wouldn't be too concerned," Aros Securities telecoms analyst Lars Larsen said.
